dates.notes: Signed on 1 April 2024 by Michelle Donelan, UK Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and Gina Raimondo, US Secretary of Commerce. The GOV.UK publication and press release are dated 2 April 2024. No renewal, modification, termination or replacement of the 2024 MOU was located. The institutions named at signature have been renamed: the UK AI Safety Institute is now the AI Security Institute, and NIST lists its centre as the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI). A separate UK-US Technology Prosperity Deal MOU of 18 September 2025 provides for cooperation between the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation and the UK AI Security Institute and is expressly non-binding. Joint UK AISI/CAISI technical work continued, with a joint preliminary assessment published by NIST on 23 July 2026.

Parallel transatlantic AI-safety cooperation in 2024; the US–EU side is a political dialogue commitment, not an MOU.

ai_provisions: The Institutes intend to develop an interoperable programme of work and approach to safety research.
They intend to develop a shared approach to model evaluations, including methodologies, infrastructures and processes.
They intend to perform at least one joint testing exercise on a publicly accessible model.
They intend to collaborate on AI safety technical research and to explore personnel exchanges.
They intend to share information across their activities, subject to national laws, regulations and contracts.
The partners intend to work with other governments on international standards for AI safety testing and related standards.
relevance.excluded_scope: Non-binding bilateral cooperation on AI safety science and institute-to-institute work. No treaty obligation, ratification, depositary, dispute settlement or enforcement; no general AI regulation or military-AI commitment.
relevance.reason: A bilateral government memorandum of understanding on AI safety science, signed on 1 April 2024 by the UK Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology and the US Secretary of Commerce. It provides the basis for cooperation between the UK and US AI Safety Institutes on model evaluations, joint testing, technical research, personnel exchanges and information sharing. It is a non-binding MOU, not a treaty, and the official GOV.UK publication is a summary of key elements rather than the full MOU text.

status_note: Bilateral memorandum of understanding between the United Kingdom and the United States. It is a non-binding political and technical cooperation instrument, not a treaty. The classification follows the MOU form and the absence of binding language in the official summary; the full MOU text was not published. The summary states no ratification, depositary, duration, termination, review or dispute-settlement procedure. No renewal, termination or replacement document was located. The institutions have since been renamed: the UK AI Safety Institute is now the AI Security Institute, and NIST lists its centre as the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI). A separate UK-US Technology Prosperity Deal MOU of 18 September 2025 provides for cooperation between the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation and the UK AI Security Institute and is expressly non-binding; it may be discontinued 180 days after notice. Joint UK AISI/CAISI technical work continued, with a joint preliminary assessment published by NIST on 23 July 2026.
